albionEmpires.description:
A web platform for Albion Online, fed by a small desktop agent that passively listens to the game's network traffic on each player's machine. It answers the question the game does not: where people have been, and what a group knows about a place over time.
The agent captures and forwards, never sending a packet to the game, reading its memory or touching its files. A Rust server decodes, stores and serves; the site draws the world map with a time slider, a kill feed with a per-fight damage meter replayed second by second, crafting costs from the game's own recipes, and an auction-house ledger.
Data is shared through pools: each account records what its agent sees, and a pool only grows by invitation. Reading several pools merges them, keeping the freshest record per entity, and nobody is ever told who observes them.

playability.description:
PlayAbility is a software that helps people with disabilities play video games again, using AI and facial recognition.
I shipped new features on the existing application and ran security audits and remediation work.

onlyone.description:
I led the redesign and development of OnlyOne, a proprietary Electron.js application consolidating game distribution services such as Steam and Blizzard into a single interface.
Beyond unifying access to those platforms, it adds social features like real-time chat and group management.
I engineered the API integrations behind it, keeping communication with external platforms reliable and predictable.

padtolan.description:
Originally built for Star Citizen, PadToLan turns any device on your LAN into a customisable touchpad.
It replicates configurable keybinds on the host, with double-tap, hold and loop behaviours.

albionAccountant.description:
An auction-house ledger for Albion Online. It follows a selling session — sales, fees, sales tax, setup fees and repairs — and works out what each player is owed once the haul is split with a guild.
Charts break the numbers down over time, by item, and by hour and weekday. A templated Discord message turns a session into a report the group can read at a glance.
It grew out of Albion OCR, a proof of concept that read sales data off the screen through text recognition.

electron.title: Electron.js
electron.lead: Why a desktop application built with Electron.js is often the fastest path to a product your users can install.
electron.benefitsTitle: What it brings to your product

benefits.title: Cross-platform by default
benefits.description: One codebase runs on Windows, macOS and Linux, so your software reaches a wider audience without extra development cost.

benefits.title: Rich desktop experience
benefits.description: Modern interfaces with smooth animations and responsive layouts, backed by the full power of current web technologies.

benefits.title: Fast iteration
benefits.description: Built on web technologies, it shortens development cycles and lets an existing web application become a desktop app quickly.

benefits.title: Native capabilities
benefits.description: Direct access to the file system, notifications, tray icons, protocols and everything the desktop environment exposes.

benefits.title: Cost effective
benefits.description: A single codebase across platforms keeps development and maintenance costs low, with no separate team per operating system.

benefits.title: Mature ecosystem
benefits.description: A large, active community means plenty of tooling and libraries, and faster answers when a challenge shows up.

benefits.title: Scalable
benefits.description: Straightforward integration with cloud services, APIs and databases, so the application grows with your business.
